summary: Most of this neighbourhood's record is about what may stand here and what may not. The Board fixed set-back lines street by street — ten feet back on one stretch of Pacific Avenue, twenty on Green Street — and it said no a great deal: to a laundry at 2209 Pine Street in 1913, a stable at 2786 California in 1916, a sanitarium at 1902 Broderick the same year, an oil tank at 2336 Webster in 1921. When it did grant G. B. Mon a French laundry on California Street in 1925 the Mayor vetoed the permit, and a neighbour came to the hearing to speak against it. What it granted freely was fuel oil: fifteen hundred gallons under one house after another, Rudolph Spreckels at 1900 Pacific Avenue, Captain William Matson at 2225 Jackson Street. After the fire it buried water too, cisterns at Laguna and Union, Buchanan and California, Greenwich and Webster, paid off in instalments through 1909. In 1907 the Fillmore Street merchants put up fourteen electric arches over their own crossings and the city switched off eighty-two arc lights in exchange. Thirty-eight horses stood behind 2113 Pine Street in 1914. Four schools were ordered in two years around 1920, and the streets outside them were roped off at playtime — Green Street from noon to one for the pastor of St Vincent de Paul, Broderick Street whenever the Grant School children were out of the building. Two streets were closed altogether in 1932 for being too steep to drive. A hospital grew in the middle of the neighbourhood and kept asking to go underneath it — Stanford's tunnel across Clay Street in 1921, and sixty years later conduits under Clay, Webster and Sacramento for the Pacific Medical Center, which came back again in 1982 for a medical office building on Webster Street. From the 1970s the neighbourhood down-zoned itself and started naming its houses instead — the Haas-Lilienthal on Franklin Street, the Atherton on California, the Madame C. J. Walker Home for Girls and Women on Pine Street — while its flats came back to the Board one condominium map at a time, and have not stopped since.
